question:
A 35-year-old woman with cystic fibrosis enrolls in hospice care due to advanced disease. She
experiences severe dyspnea requiring frequent doses of morphine for relief. Her pulmonologist
estimates she has only a few weeks to live. While prioritizing comfort, she wishes to remain as alert as
possible. She begins to experience involuntary jerking movements of her arms and legs, which are
distressing to her and her family. What is the most appropriate treatment for her myoclonus? Answer
Choices: (A) Start a midazolam infusion. (B) Start clonazepam. (C) Reduce morphine dose by 50%. (D)
Add gabapentin to current regimen. (E) Start valproic acid. (F) Start levetiracetam therapy. (G) Add
baclofen to current regimen. (H) Switch to fentanyl patch. (I) Replace morphine with hydromorphone.
(J) Start diazepam therapy.
 A. Start valproic acid.
B. Switch to fentanyl patch.
C. Add baclofen to current regimen.
D. Start clonazepam.
E. Start levetiracetam therapy.
F. Start a midazolam infusion.

G. Start diazepam therapy.
H. Add gabapentin to current regimen.
I. Reduce morphine dose by 50%.
J. Replace morphine with hydromorphone.
